---

**TOP LINE**
Treasury's Title VI rescission rule, published August 3, aligns regulations more closely with statutory text and an executive order. Monitor H.R. 9768 (Tariff Refund Act) and H.R. 9761 (Disclosure of Tax Havens Act) for revenue and IRC Section 6103 confidentiality implications. Several parallel House and Senate bills targeting high-income retirement account balances raise significant IRS implementation risk.

---

**NOMINATIONS**
Four nominees are floor-scheduled: Browne (Under Secretary), Brooke (Deputy Secretary), and McMasters and Kothari (both Assistant Secretaries). Gadwood (IRS Chief Counsel) remains in committee at 40 days. Kothari carries a prior return at 211 days. Korb, Trennert, and Petit were withdrawn.

---

**LEGISLATION & RULES**
Active bills with Treasury equities include H.R. 9978 (homeowner insurance premium deduction), S. 5142 (IRS refund process), S. 5144 (installment agreement fees), H.R. 9801 (ABLE MATCH), and companion retirement cap bills S. 5040 and H.R. 9813. H.R. 8823 and S.Res. 805 present no Treasury equities.

---

**HEARINGS**
House Financial Services Subcommittee: Oversight of FinCEN. Witness: Director Andrea Gacki.

# House Financial Services Committee — Democratic Member Prep Sheet
## Witness Topic: Corporate Transparency Act / BOI, AML Modernization, Crypto Illicit Finance

---

## MAXINE WATERS (D-CA) — Ranking Member

**Line 1:** Waters will likely press on FinCEN's enforcement posture following court-ordered CTA suspensions, asking whether Treasury is actively defending the statute and what interim steps protect the AML framework during litigation delays.

**Line 2:** She will likely raise racial economic justice framing, questioning whether shell company opacity disproportionately harms minority communities through predatory real estate purchases and whether BOI implementation addresses that harm.

**Suggested Posture:** Affirm Treasury's commitment to defending the CTA's constitutionality, cite specific enforcement actions taken during the suspension period, and acknowledge the community impact dimension without overpromising on litigation outcomes.

---

## NYDIA M. VELÁZQUEZ (D-NY)

**Line 1:** Velázquez will likely focus on small business compliance burden, particularly for minority-owned and immigrant-owned small businesses that may lack legal infrastructure to navigate BOI filing requirements and deadlines.

**Line 2:** She will likely question whether FinCEN's outreach to underserved business communities has been adequate, citing her longstanding small business advocacy and the risk that penalties fall disproportionately on good-faith non-filers.

**Suggested Posture:** Lead with FinCEN's multilingual outreach efforts and penalty waiver guidance for first-time filers, emphasize the 23 exemption categories, and offer to provide the member's office with jurisdiction-specific compliance data.

---

## BRAD SHERMAN (D-CA)

**Line 1:** Sherman will likely pursue technical crypto illicit finance questions, particularly on decentralized finance and whether Treasury's existing BSA authorities are legally sufficient to cover DeFi protocols without new legislation.

**Line 2:** He will likely ask about the adequacy of the cryptocurrency travel rule implementation, pressing on whether foreign virtual asset service providers serving U.S. customers are subject to equivalent AML obligations.

**Suggested Posture:** Engage the technical specificity directly, cite the 2023 and 2024 FinCEN crypto advisories, acknowledge jurisdictional gaps in VASP coverage honestly, and indicate Treasury's position on legislative needs without prejudging congressional deliberations.

---

## GREGORY W. MEEKS (D-NY)

**Line 1:** Meeks will likely raise international coordination concerns, asking whether U.S. BOI standards align with FATF recommendations and whether peer jurisdictions' more advanced beneficial ownership registries create competitive or enforcement disadvantages.

**Line 2:** He will likely question how Treasury is working with correspondent banking partners and foreign financial intelligence units to leverage BOI data for cross-border illicit finance investigations.

**Suggested Posture:** Reference U.S. FATF mutual evaluation outcomes, highlight the Egmont Group information-sharing framework, and emphasize that the BOI registry positions the United States to meet international standards after years of criticism for lagging behind allies.

---

## STEPHEN F. LYNCH (D-MA)

**Line 1:** Lynch, as a former chair of the Financial Technology Task Force, will likely probe FinCEN's supervisory examination findings on AML program deficiencies at banks and whether those deficiencies are concentrated in specific institution types or asset sizes.

**Line 2:** He will likely question Treasury's approach to emerging payment systems and Central Bank Digital Currency AML implications, given his consistent interest in fintech oversight architecture.

**Suggested Posture:** Provide concrete SAR filing trend data, reference the AML Act of 2020 implementation milestones, and give a measured, factually grounded answer on CBDC AML design considerations while noting that policy decisions remain under review.

---

## AL GREEN (D-TX)

**Line 1:** Green will likely press on whether illicit finance tools including shell companies are being used specifically in housing markets in communities of color and whether Treasury is coordinating with HUD or DOJ on targeted enforcement.

**Line 2:** He will likely raise concerns about discriminatory patterns in financial institution AML suspicious activity reporting, asking whether SARs are filed disproportionately on minority customers and what Treasury oversight exists for that risk.

**Suggested Posture:** Acknowledge the intersection of fair lending and AML compliance risk, cite any interagency coordination with DOJ and HUD, and commit to providing data on geographic targeting of real estate AML orders if available at the unclassified level.

---

## EMANUEL CLEAVER (D-MO)

**Line 1:** Cleaver will likely frame questions around community development financial institutions and smaller financial entities, asking whether AML compliance costs create undue barriers for CDFIs serving underbanked populations.

**Line 2:** He may raise the spiritual or ethical dimension of financial crime harm in plain language, then pivot to a practical question about whether Treasury's AML modernization reduces friction for legitimate small-dollar transactions flagged in error.

**Suggested Posture:** Acknowledge CDFI compliance burden concerns directly, cite the FinCEN SAR and CTR threshold review process under the AML Act of 2020, and affirm that modernization aims to increase signal quality and reduce burden on low-risk community institutions.

---

## JAMES A. HIMES (D-CT)

**Line 1:** Himes, with an intelligence and national security background, will likely ask about the classified or law enforcement utility of BOI data, specifically whether the registry has produced actionable leads in national security investigations and how access controls function.

**Line 2:** He will likely press on the adequacy of Treasury's OFAC and FinCEN coordination on sanctions evasion through crypto assets, particularly following Russia-related enforcement actions.

**Suggested Posture:** Offer to provide a classified or law enforcement sensitive briefing for specifics on investigative utility, confirm that access to the BOI database is restricted to authorized law enforcement under defined protocols, and cite publicly available OFAC crypto enforcement statistics.

## BILL FOSTER (D-IL)

**Line 1:** Foster, a physicist with deep technology fluency, will likely probe the cryptographic and database security architecture of the FinCEN BOI registry, asking whether it is resilient to data breaches and whether zero-trust or encryption standards have been applied.

**Line 2:** He will likely ask technically specific questions about blockchain analytics tools used by Treasury, whether those tools are validated for accuracy, and what the false positive rate is in transaction monitoring that flags illicit activity.

**Suggested Posture:** Engage the technical questions at an appropriate level of specificity,

bills.title: Homeowners Premium Tax Reduction Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9978 directly implicates the Internal Revenue Service and Treasury's Office of Tax Policy because it would create or expand a tax deduction or credit reducing federal revenue from homeowner insurance premiums. Treasury must assess the static and dynamic revenue cost, design anti-abuse rules, and determine IRS administrative capacity to verify eligible premium payments at scale.

bills.title: A bill to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to improve the process for providing refunds to taxpayers.
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
bills.nexus: S. 5142 directly implicates IRS authority under Title 26 and falls within the jurisdiction of the Office of Tax Policy, which would need to assess any statutory changes to refund procedures, timelines, or interest accrual rules. Treasury's implementation risk centers on IRS operational capacity and systems readiness to execute revised refund processes, as well as potential budgetary exposure if accelerated refund timelines increase improper payment vulnerability.

bills.title: A bill to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to eliminate installment agreement fees for certain individuals.
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
bills.nexus: S. 5144 directly affects IRS revenue collection operations under Treasury's tax administration authority, as installment agreement user fees are set and collected pursuant to IRC Section 6159 and related Office of Management and Budget cost-recovery guidance. Eliminating fees for certain taxpayers would reduce IRS offsetting collections, requiring Treasury and IRS to assess the fiscal impact and determine whether appropriated funds or restructured fee schedules for other filers must compensate for the lost revenue.

bills.title: ABLE MATCH (Making Able a Tool to Combat Hardship) Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9801 directly implicates Treasury's Office of Tax Policy and IRS because ABLE accounts are tax-advantaged savings vehicles governed under IRC Section 529A, making Treasury the primary regulatory authority for any statutory changes to contribution rules or matching incentives. The implementation risk centers on IRS's responsibility to issue guidance, update Form 5498-QA reporting requirements, and coordinate with states administering ABLE programs to operationalize any new federal matching structure.

bills.title: A bill to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to impose limitations on high-income taxpayers with large retirement account balances.
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
bills.nexus: S. 5040 directly implicates IRS and Treasury's Office of Tax Policy, as it would amend the Internal Revenue Code to cap retirement account balances for high-income individuals and trigger required distributions or contribution prohibitions above set thresholds. Treasury faces significant implementation risk because the proposal would require new IRS guidance, reporting infrastructure, and enforcement mechanisms to identify and act on out-of-compliance balances across multiple account types.

bills.title: To amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to impose limitations on high-income taxpayers with large retirement account balances.
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9813 directly implicates IRS and Treasury's Office of Tax Policy, as it would amend the Internal Revenue Code to cap tax-advantaged retirement balances for high-income earners. Treasury faces significant implementation risk around required minimum distribution rule changes, valuation methodologies for non-publicly traded assets, and IRS enforcement capacity to monitor account thresholds at scale.

bills.title: Putting Patients First by Strengthening Provider Accountability in FECA Act
bills.status: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
bills.nexus: H.R. 8823 amends the Federal Employees' Compensation Act (FECA), which is administered by the Department of Labor, not Treasury, and its provider accountability provisions do not implicate Treasury's tax, fiscal, or financial regulatory authorities. Treasury should monitor for any appropriations or payment integrity provisions that could affect federal workers' compensation outlays scored against the federal budget, but absent a known nexus, this bill presents no direct Treasury equities at this stage.

bills.title: Tariff Refund Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus:
Without a known nexus provided, here is a placeholder brief based on the bill title alone:

H.R. 9768 would require refunds of collected tariff revenues, directly implicating U.S. Customs and Border Protection's revenue collections and Treasury's authority over the Customs Revenue Function under 19 U.S.C. The implementation risk centers on the Office of Tax Policy and CBP coordinating refund mechanisms, potential revenue scoring impacts on the federal budget, and administrative burden on the customs drawback system.

bills.title: Disclosure of Tax Havens and Offshoring Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Financial Services.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9761 would require public country-by-country reporting of corporate tax and financial data, directly implicating IRS authority under the Internal Revenue Code and Treasury's tax policy office (Office of Tax Policy). Treasury's implementation risk centers on reconciling new public disclosure mandates with existing taxpayer confidentiality rules under IRC Section 6103 and coordinating with SEC rulemaking given the bill's referral to Financial Services.

bills.title: HONOR Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: Without a confirmed nexus on file, I can flag the referral angle: Ways and Means jurisdiction signals the bill likely touches tax expenditures, tariffs, or trade, all areas where Treasury's Office of Tax Policy or the Office of Tariff Affairs and Trade Agreements would have equities. Treasury should monitor for any revenue scoring implications or regulatory implementation duties that could fall to IRS or USTR coordination.

bills.title: A resolution celebrating the historic significance of the 2026 Federation Internationale de Football Association (FIFA) World Cup and welcoming the international community to North America for the first tournament hosted by 3 nations.
bills.status: Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent. (consideration: CR S4117; text: CR S4109)
bills.nexus: S.Res. 805 is a purely celebratory Senate resolution with no legislative text creating new law, appropriations, or regulatory authority, meaning it touches no Treasury office or statutory mandate. Treasury has no implementation role and faces no fiscal or regulatory risk from this measure.

bills.title: HONOR Act
bills.nexus: S. 327, the HONOR Act, is held at the desk with no confirmed nexus to Treasury's statutory authorities or program offices yet identified. Until referral or legislative text confirms a hook to tax administration, sanctions, AML/CFT, debt management, or financial stability, Treasury has no clear implementation obligation or regulatory risk to flag.
